title: Requisites of a Valid Adoption — Section 6 HAMA

content.overview: Section 6 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 sets the conditions for a valid adoption. No adoption is valid unless the person adopting has the capacity and right to take in adoption; the person giving in adoption has the capacity to do so; the person adopted is capable of being taken in adoption; and the adoption is made in compliance with the other conditions of the Chapter (including ss. 7–11).
content.glance: Ask: (1) Capacity of adopter? (2) Capacity of giver? (3) Capacity of adoptee? (4) Other Chapter conditions (ss. 7–11) met?
content.study:
Section 6 is the gateway provision. Failure of any of the four conditions invalidates the adoption.

Capacity of the male and female adopter is detailed in ss. 7–8; capacity to give in ss. 9; who may be adopted in s. 10; other conditions (age difference, prohibition of simultaneous adoption of two, ceremonies, etc.) in s. 11.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Four conditions
sections.body: Capacity to take; capacity to give; capacity to be taken; compliance with other Chapter conditions.

sections.heading: Link to ss. 7–8
sections.body: Male and female capacity and right to adopt.

sections.heading: Link to s. 9
sections.body: Who may give in adoption (father, mother, guardian with court permission where required).

sections.heading: Link to s. 10
sections.body: Who may be adopted (Hindu, not already adopted, unmarried and under fifteen unless custom).

sections.heading: Link to s. 11
sections.body: Other conditions including age gap, single child of same sex, actual giving and taking.

examples.title: Missing capacity
examples.body: Person without capacity under ss. 7–8 purports to adopt — adoption invalid under s. 6.

hypotheticals.question: Is a ceremony alone enough for a valid adoption under HAMA?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. All four s. 6 conditions must be satisfied, including capacity rules and s. 11 conditions.

distinctions.title: s. 6 validity vs s. 12 effects
distinctions.right: Legal effects once valid (ties with family of birth severed, etc.).

misconceptions.trap: Any Hindu can adopt any child without further conditions.
misconceptions.correction: s. 6 requires capacity of all parties and compliance with ss. 7–11.
